title: Broderie anglaise
summary: Broderie anglaise is white cotton whitework. Small round and oval holes are punched or cut and edged with close overcast stitches, and leaves and petals are filled in satin stitch, often along a scalloped edge. Light and cool, it trims cuffs, collars and summer dresses.
howToPlay: Pick a thread colour from the reels and an eyelet shape from the tray.
Touch a square on the cloth to work that shape there; it is mirrored across and down.
Copy the border shown on the card, then press Check.
rules: The border is mirrored left to right and top to bottom, so every shape you work is also worked on its partner squares.
A square counts only when its shape and its thread colour both match the border you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: English eyelet embroidery became popular in the mid-nineteenth century, when it was used for underclothes, children’s clothes and summer wear, and later for machine-made trimmings. It is still stitched by hand for christening gowns, collars and table linen.
